\section[asegurar]{asegurar — to assure, to insist; to insure}

\label{lesson:ES-C516-asegurar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to declare, then the Spanish for to confirm.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: asegurar}
\textbf{asegurar} — \textquotedblleft{}to assure, to insist; to insure\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Me aseguró que no había visto nada.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He assured me that he had not seen anything.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Asegurarse de algo} is to make sure of it. \emph{Asegurar el coche} is to insure the car.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{asegurar} is built on \emph{seguro} 'sure, safe' with the prefix \emph{a-}. \emph{Seguro} is inherited from Latin \emph{sēcūrus} (EtymDB), 'free from care', from \emph{sē-} 'without' and \emph{cūra} 'care' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{asegurar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{asegurar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to declare, then the Spanish for to confirm, then say \emph{asegurar} again
\end{itemize}

\section[rectificar]{rectificar — to correct, to put right}

\label{lesson:ES-C516-rectificar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to confirm, then the Spanish for to assure.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: rectificar}
\textbf{rectificar} — \textquotedblleft{}to correct, to put right\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Un día después, el periódico rectificó la noticia.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{A day later, the newspaper corrected the story.}
\end{quote}

It takes \emph{qu} before \emph{e}: \emph{rectifiqué}. \emph{Rectificar es de sabios} — it is wise to admit a mistake.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{rectificar} is usually traced to Late Latin \emph{rēctificāre} 'to make straight', a learned word built on \emph{rēctus} 'straight' (Lewis \& Short) and \emph{facere} 'to make'. To correct a story is to set it straight.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to confirm, then the Spanish for to assure, then say \emph{rectificar} again
\end{itemize}

\section[revelar]{revelar — to reveal; to develop (a photo)}

\label{lesson:ES-C516-revelar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to assure, then the Spanish for to correct.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: revelar}
\textbf{revelar} — \textquotedblleft{}to reveal; to develop (a photo)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El periódico reveló el nombre del ladrón.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The newspaper revealed the thief's name.}
\end{quote}

With old film, \emph{revelar las fotos} is to develop the photos.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{revelar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{revēlāre} 'to draw back the veil' (EtymDB), built on \emph{re-} and \emph{vēlum} 'a cloth, a veil'. To reveal is to pull the cloth away.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[desmentir]{desmentir — to refute, to deny publicly}

\label{lesson:ES-C516-desmentir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to correct, then the Spanish for to reveal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: desmentir}
\textbf{desmentir} — \textquotedblleft{}to refute, to deny publicly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El club desmintió la noticia.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The club denied the story.}
\end{quote}

Used for rumours and news reports. Stem change: \emph{desmiento}, \emph{desmintió}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{desmentir} is built on \emph{mentir} 'to lie' with the prefix \emph{des-}. \emph{Mentir} is inherited from Latin \emph{mentīrī} 'to lie' (EtymDB). To desmentir a story is to call it a lie.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to correct, then the Spanish for to reveal, then say \emph{desmentir} again

\section[la versión]{la versión — the version, the account}

\label{lesson:ES-C516-version}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to reveal, then the Spanish for to refute.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la versión}
\textbf{la versión} — \textquotedblleft{}the version, the account\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Cada persona tiene su versión de lo que pasó.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Each person has their own version of what happened.}
\end{quote}

\emph{En versión original} on a cinema listing means not dubbed.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{versión} is a learned borrowing from Medieval Latin \emph{versiō} 'a turning, a translation' (EtymDB), built on \emph{vertere} 'to turn'. A version is a story turned one particular way.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
